intro: Hearing aid specialists fit devices, teach patients and build long-term trust, skills used across health care. The closest of the 25 careers below is Dental Assistants, with a 79% skill match, while Audiologists are a 69% match with a BLS May 2025 median of $95,780, or 47% more than the $65,160 specialists earn.
why_it_works: Your work mixes testing, adjusting equipment and explaining results to patients who may be worried. O*NET rates service orientation at 3.62 out of 5 for this job and instructing at 3.5. Therapy assistant, respiratory and audiology roles use that same patient teaching. Some matches need more schooling. The skills to grow are leading staff, running equipment and analyzing how a clinic runs.
tips: Audiology is the natural step up, but it needs a doctoral degree; check program length before you commit.
Respiratory Therapists earn $82,280, which is 26% more, after an associate-level program.
Track how many fittings you complete and your patient return rate; clinics value proven results.

faq.q: What jobs can former hearing aid specialists do?
faq.a: The closest matches are Dental Assistants (79%), Physical Therapist Assistants (72%) and Audiologists (69%), based on O*NET 31.0. Physical Therapist Assistants earn $68,380, which is 5% more than the $65,160 hearing aid specialist median, and usually need an associate degree.

faq.q: Which careers for hearing aid specialists pay more?
faq.a: 10 of the 25 matches pay more. Radiation Therapists earn $105,310 (62% more), Registered Nurses $97,550 (50% more) and Audiologists $95,780 (47% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Each of these needs a specific degree program and a state license.

faq.q: Do hearing aid specialists need more education to switch?
faq.a: For many paths. 19 of the 25 matches need no more education than specialists already have, but only 1 needs a graduate degree. In the closest match, 46% of workers hold a post-secondary certificate, and therapy assistants usually have an associate degree.

faq.q: What skills should hearing aid specialists build?
faq.a: The skills that most often need work are social perceptiveness, managing people, operation and control and operations analysis. Complex problem solving already rates 3.12 out of 5 for this job in O*NET, so clinical depth and running a practice are the main next steps.
